messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): freq, knee_amp, torque_limit, torso_mass, foot_length, hip_amp, kd, foot_friction, kp, leg_density, pitch_kp, leg_length, balance_gain, ramp_s
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): start_lean, pitch_ref, fp_kv, knee_shift, hip_bias, stance_knee, sync_gain, fp_kd, duty
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: friction_utilisation_p95, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pitch_end, pitch_rate_end, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, n_walking, capture_margin_over_L_slope, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, capture_inside_fraction, tracking_error_knee, angmom_norm_end, capture_margin_over_L_end, fall_time, slip_fraction, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, n_fell, pitch_rate_mean, pre_fall.pitch, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, angmom_norm_mean, com_vx_mean, time_upright, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, pre_fall.slip_fraction, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_vx, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, angmom_norm_slope, flight_fraction, pre_fall.angmom_norm, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, tracking_error_hip, pitch_rate_slope, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, step_freq_hz, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, com_vx_end, double_support_fraction, pitch_slope, com_vx_slope, tracking_error_ankle, step_length_over_L, swing_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_height_over_L_end, pitch_mean, saturation_frac_hip, saturation_frac_knee, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

STEP 1 of at most 12. Model requests used so far: 0 of 24.
Rollout budget: 696 remaining of 700; n_obs = 4, n_train = 4.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): freq, knee_amp, torque_limit, torso_mass, foot_length, hip_amp, kd, foot_friction, kp, leg_density, pitch_kp, leg_length, balance_gain, ramp_s
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): start_lean, pitch_ref, fp_kv, knee_shift, hip_bias, stance_knee, sync_gain, fp_kd, duty
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: friction_utilisation_p95, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pitch_end, pitch_rate_end, capture_margin_over_L_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, n_walking, capture_margin_over_L_slope, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, capture_inside_fraction, tracking_error_knee, angmom_norm_end, capture_margin_over_L_end, fall_time, slip_fraction, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, n_fell, pitch_rate_mean, pre_fall.pitch, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, angmom_norm_mean, com_vx_mean, time_upright, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, pre_fall.slip_fraction, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_vx, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, angmom_norm_slope, flight_fraction, pre_fall.angmom_norm, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, tracking_error_hip, pitch_rate_slope, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, step_freq_hz, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, com_vx_end, double_support_fraction, pitch_slope, com_vx_slope, tracking_error_ankle, step_length_over_L, swing_clearance_min_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_height_over_L_end, pitch_mean, saturation_frac_hip, saturation_frac_knee, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): torque_limit, hip_amp, knee_amp, kd, leg_density, foot_friction, kp, balance_gain, freq, foot_length, ramp_s, torso_mass, leg_length, pitch_kp
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): hip_bias, duty, fp_kd, pitch_ref, sync_gain, stance_knee, knee_shift, start_lean, fp_kv
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: friction_utilisation_p95, pre_fall.pitch, com_vx_end, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, flight_fraction, pitch_end, swing_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.pitch_rate, slip_fraction, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, pitch_rate_mean, step_length_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_slope, time_upright, angmom_norm_slope, fall_time, tracking_error_knee, capture_margin_over_L_end, tracking_error_hip, capture_margin_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pitch_rate_slope, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, capture_inside_fraction, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, n_walking, tracking_error_ankle, step_freq_hz, pre_fall.slip_fraction, saturation_frac_hip, com_vx_mean, pitch_slope, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, n_fell, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, com_vx_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pitch_mean, saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.angmom_norm, com_height_over_L_mean, double_support_fraction, angmom_norm_end, com_height_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_vx. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): torque_limit, hip_amp, knee_amp, kd, leg_density, foot_friction, kp, balance_gain, freq, foot_length, ramp_s, torso_mass, leg_length, pitch_kp
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): hip_bias, duty, fp_kd, pitch_ref, sync_gain, stance_knee, knee_shift, start_lean, fp_kv
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: friction_utilisation_p95, pre_fall.pitch, com_vx_end, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, flight_fraction, pitch_end, swing_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.pitch_rate, slip_fraction, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, pitch_rate_mean, step_length_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_slope, time_upright, angmom_norm_slope, fall_time, tracking_error_knee, capture_margin_over_L_end, tracking_error_hip, capture_margin_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pitch_rate_slope, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, capture_inside_fraction, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, n_walking, tracking_error_ankle, step_freq_hz, pre_fall.slip_fraction, saturation_frac_hip, com_vx_mean, pitch_slope, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, n_fell, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, com_vx_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pitch_mean, saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.angmom_norm, com_height_over_L_mean, double_support_fraction, angmom_norm_end, com_height_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_vx. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kd, leg_length, foot_length, freq, foot_friction, torque_limit, knee_amp, balance_gain, pitch_kp, kp, ramp_s, hip_amp, leg_density, torso_mass
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, pitch_ref, fp_kd, fp_kv, hip_bias, stance_knee, start_lean, knee_shift, sync_gain
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kd, leg_length, foot_length, freq, foot_friction, torque_limit, knee_amp, balance_gain, pitch_kp, kp, ramp_s, hip_amp, leg_density, torso_mass
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, pitch_ref, fp_kd, fp_kv, hip_bias, stance_knee, start_lean, knee_shift, sync_gain
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain

final.explanation: The primary observable defect is an overly long stance phase (high duty) producing short steps and low forward speed, which destabilises the capture point. Correcting duty via the timing tool should lengthen swing, increase step length and forward COM velocity, improving balance. A secondary contribution comes from insufficient leg inertia relative to torso mass; increasing leg length via the leg_length tool raises leg leverage and inertia, mitigating the rearward pitch bias.

H1.causal_chain: High duty → shorter swing → reduced step length → lower forward COM velocity → inadequate capture point regulation → falls forward when momentum insufficient, falls backward when excessive braking from prolonged stance.
H1.mechanism: Excessive duty cycle (stance too long) reduces swing duration, yielding short step lengths and insufficient forward momentum, leading to loss of balance and bidirectional falls.

H2.causal_chain: Low leg density ↓ leg inertia & torque capacity → torso pitches backward (negative pitch) → COM shifts rearward → capture point moves backward → increased tendency to fall backward; compensatory forward stepping attempts produce forward falls.
H2.mechanism: Legs are too light relative to the torso (low leg density, high torso fraction) causing a rearward pitch bias and inadequate ground‑reaction forward impulse, compromising balance.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): hip_amp, leg_length, torso_mass, leg_density, kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, foot_friction, knee_amp, foot_length, ramp_s, torque_limit, freq
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, stance_knee, pitch_ref, sync_gain, hip_bias, knee_shift, fp_kv, start_lean, duty
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_end, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, pitch_rate_end, tracking_error_hip, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, fall_time, step_length_over_L, com_height_over_L_slope, pitch_rate_slope, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, com_vx_slope, pre_fall.angmom_norm, pitch_mean, pitch_rate_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, com_height_over_L_end, angmom_norm_end, com_vx_end, friction_utilisation_p95, pitch_slope, n_fell, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, saturation_frac_hip, saturation_frac_ankle, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, capture_margin_over_L_mean, angmom_norm_slope, n_walking, capture_inside_fraction, step_freq_hz, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, saturation_frac_knee, com_vx_mean, slip_fraction, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.com_vx, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, double_support_fraction, swing_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, max_friction_utilisation, flight_fraction, time_upright, capture_margin_over_L_slope, pre_fall.slip_fraction, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.pitch, pitch_end, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.
